From a claim to evidence: a complete CSDG walkthrough

Source: vignettes/claim_scoped_diagnostic_gates.Rmd
claim_scoped_diagnostic_gates.Rmd

This guide follows the five steps of the accompanying article: write the claim, specify the scope, derive the required properties, evaluate the evidence, and decide and report. The input is a claim, a conclusion that a researcher intends to report. The output is its assessment (met, not met, or unresolved) and a decision: a met claim is retained; a claim that is not met or unresolved is revised or withheld. The package records the claim and its scope, derives the gate plan, computes diagnostics, and applies the decision rule. The researcher sets the criteria, states the relevance of each observation, and enters established counterevidence and unresolved threats.

All code runs on generated data; no SHILD or PISA files are needed. The first part works through the numerical example of the article. The second part applies the steps to a fitted mlr3 learner and shows an unresolved claim with an unresolved threat.

library(mlr3autoiml)
library(data.table)
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3learners)
library(mlr3pipelines)
packageVersion("mlr3autoiml")
#> [1] '0.1.6'

Step 1: Write the claim

Suppose that two items, for example two wordings of the self-rated health question, carry the same information. For exact arithmetic, let Z be standard normal, let both items and the outcome equal Z, and use squared error. Model A is f_A(x) = x1 and model B is f_B(x) = x2, both defined for all inputs and without error. The claim is:

Under marginal permutation, both models rely more on item 1 than on item 2.

The record states that the claim was written before the values were computed (specified in advance).

Step 2: Specify the scope

The scope states what the claim refers to, in six elements: the quantity (the estimand that the claim interprets), the model, the procedure (the estimator that computes the quantity), the data, the meaning (model description, population claim, or causal claim), and the use.

claim_both = csdg_claim(
  id = "both_models",
  statement = "Under marginal permutation, both models rely more on item 1 than on item 2.",
  claim_type = "global_explanation",
  quantity = "marginal PFI with squared error: increase in expected squared error when one item is permuted",
  model = "several_models",
  procedure = paste(
    "each item permuted independently of the other item and the outcome;",
    "20 permutations per held-out fold of a 5-fold cross-validation"
  ),
  data = "population Z ~ N(0, 1), item 1 = item 2 = outcome = Z; 10,000 simulated observations",
  meaning = "model_description",
  use = "scientific description",
  unit = "simulated observation",
  population = "Z standard normal",
  provenance = list(origin = "specified_before_results", date = "2026-09-26",
    time_basis = "date of the example", selection_basis = "written before the PFI values were computed",
    evidence_ids = character())
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(element = names(claim_both$scope), content = unlist(claim_both$scope)),
  row.names = FALSE)
element content
quantity marginal PFI with squared error: increase in expected squared error when one item is permuted
model several_models
procedure each item permuted independently of the other item and the outcome; 20 permutations per held-out fold of a 5-fold cross-validation
data population Z ~ N(0, 1), item 1 = item 2 = outcome = Z; 10,000 simulated observations
meaning model_description
use scientific description

Marginal permutation creates input combinations that never occur in the data: a permuted input has unequal items. A model description may cover such inputs if its scope says so, as must its reported wording. The qualifier “under marginal permutation” is therefore part of the claim; without it, the claim would be broader than its scope.

measurement = csdg_measurement(
  outcome = "y", predictors = c("item_1", "item_2"),
  data_source = "simulated from the specified population",
  sample_definition = "all simulated observations; no exclusions",
  unit = "simulated observation", outcome_scale = "continuous, variance one",
  missingness = "none", preprocessing = "none"
)
groups = list(item_1 = "item_1", item_2 = "item_2", both_items = c("item_1", "item_2"))
explanation = csdg_explanation(
  method_ids = "pfi", scope = "global", target = "prediction", feature_groups = groups,
  perturbation = list(type = "marginal", distribution = "held-out fold")
)

Step 3: Derive the required properties

A gate is a generic evidence question, such as “Does the result hold for all models the claim covers?” Applied to a claim, it becomes a required property, such as “item 1 has the larger PFI in model B.” The package derives the gate plan from the column “Required if the claim …” of the gate registry (Table 3 of the article).

plan = csdg_gate_plan(claim_both, measurement, explanation)
knitr::kable(plan[, .(gate_id, gate_name, required, plan_role, trigger)])
gate_id gate_name required plan_role trigger
G0a Specification TRUE required Every claim requires a stated claim and six scope elements.
G0b Measurement and data TRUE required Every claim requires measures, sample, and outcome coding that cover what it names.
G1 Predictive performance FALSE context The claim is a model description and uses no predictions; held-out performance is context, because a model description holds whatever the model’s accuracy.
G2 Procedure TRUE required The claim interprets an explanation result (PFI).
G3a Calibration FALSE not_required The claim does not interpret predicted values as probabilities or risks.
G3b Decisions FALSE not_required The claim supports no decision about people.
G4 Local fidelity FALSE not_required The claim does not explain individual predictions.
G5 Stability TRUE required The claim states a ranking, size, or pattern of an explanation result.
G6a Models TRUE required The claim covers several models or learners.
G6b Settings FALSE not_required The claim is restricted to the sampled setting.
G7a Subgroups FALSE not_required The claim refers to no subgroup.
G7b Users FALSE not_required The claim asserts no understanding or benefit for users. 
stopifnot(identical(plan[required == TRUE, gate_id], c("G0a", "G0b", "G2", "G5", "G6a")))

Besides G0a and G0b, the claim requires G2 (it interprets PFI values), G5 (it states an ordering), and G6a (it covers two models). Held-out performance (G1) is context: a model description holds whatever the model’s accuracy.

Step 4: Evaluate the evidence

In model A, shuffling item 1 replaces the prediction Z with an independent draw Z' from the same distribution, so the expected squared error rises from 0 to E[(Z - Z')^2] = Var(Z) + Var(Z') = 2; shuffling item 2 leaves the prediction unchanged, so its PFI is 0. In model B, the values are reversed. These are exact population values. The package computes them approximately from 10,000 simulated observations: each model is a linear model of one item, which reproduces the outcome exactly in every fold.

set.seed(260926)
n = 10000L
z = rnorm(n)
task = as_task_regr(data.frame(item_1 = z, item_2 = z, y = z), target = "y", id = "numerical_example")
model_using = function(item) {
  as_learner(po("select", selector = selector_name(item), id = paste0("use_", item)) %>>% lrn("regr.lm"))
}
folds = rsmp("cv", folds = 5L)
fits = list(
  A = csdg_resample(task, model_using("item_1"), folds, measures = msrs("regr.mse"), seed = 1L),
  B = csdg_resample(task, model_using("item_2"), folds, measures = msrs("regr.mse"), seed = 1L)
)
pfi = lapply(fits, csdg_fold_pfi, feature_groups = groups, loss = "mse", repetitions = 20L, seed = 2L)
marginal = dcast(rbindlist(lapply(names(pfi), function(model) {
  pfi[[model]]$summary[, .(model = model, feature_group, mean_importance)]
})), model ~ feature_group, value.var = "mean_importance")
knitr::kable(marginal, digits = 3,
  caption = "Held-out PFI with squared error; the exact values are (2, 0) in A and (0, 2) in B.")
Held-out PFI with squared error; the exact values are (2, 0) in A and (0, 2) in B.
model both_items item_1 item_2
A 1.995 2.001 0.000
B 1.996 0.000 1.996 
stopifnot(marginal[model == "A", item_1 > item_2], marginal[model == "B", item_1 < item_2])

The Monte Carlo rule decides whether a difference is beyond the error due to random permutation: its absolute value must exceed the .975 quantile of the t distribution with R - 1 degrees of freedom times its Monte Carlo standard error, where R is the number of permutations. This rule screens out permutation noise, not sampling uncertainty. In model A, the difference between the items exceeds it in every fold. The corrected resampled t interval of the learner-level mean difference is reported descriptively.

mc_a = csdg_pfi_mc_difference(pfi$A, "item_1", "item_2")
knitr::kable(mc_a[, .(iteration, estimate, se, threshold, beyond_monte_carlo_error)], digits = 4)
iteration estimate se threshold beyond_monte_carlo_error
1 2.0625 0.0102 0.0212 TRUE
2 1.8791 0.0111 0.0231 TRUE
3 2.0229 0.0104 0.0217 TRUE
4 2.0357 0.0105 0.0219 TRUE
5 2.0037 0.0125 0.0261 TRUE 
stopifnot(all(mc_a$beyond_monte_carlo_error))
interval_a = csdg_learner_pfi_interval(pfi$A, n_train = 8000, feature_group = "item_1", minus = "item_2")
knitr::kable(interval_a[, .(estimate, se, lower, upper, df)], digits = 4)
estimate se lower upper df
2.0008 0.0478 1.8679 2.1336 4

Other versions of PFI answer other questions. Conditional PFI draws the permuted item from its distribution given the other item and so keeps the inputs realistic; because the items are equal, the draw equals the original value, and conditional PFI is 0 for both items in both models. Here, permuting within strata of Z implements this. Grouped PFI, which shuffles both items together, is about 2 in both models (the column both_items above).

conditional = lapply(fits, csdg_fold_pfi, feature_groups = groups[1:2], loss = "mse", repetitions = 5L,
  strata = z, seed = 3L)
conditional_table = dcast(rbindlist(lapply(names(conditional), function(model) {
  conditional[[model]]$summary[, .(model = model, feature_group, mean_importance)]
})), model ~ feature_group, value.var = "mean_importance")
knitr::kable(conditional_table, digits = 3, caption = "Conditional PFI.")
Conditional PFI.
model item_1 item_2
A 0 0
B 0 0 
stopifnot(all(abs(as.matrix(conditional_table[, .(item_1, item_2)])) < 1e-12))

For each required property, the record contains four entries: the property, the criterion that decides whether it holds, the observation, and its relevance. Judged against its criterion, each required property is supported, contradicted, or open.

property = function(gate_id, status, required_property, observation, relevance, criterion = NULL) {
  csdg_evidence_record(
    gate_id, TRUE, "required_property", status = status,
    criterion = if (!is.null(criterion)) list(value = criterion, direction = "qualitative"),
    criterion_source = if (!is.null(criterion)) "translated from the claim",
    criterion_rationale = if (!is.null(criterion)) required_property,
    rationale = observation, required_property = required_property, observation = observation,
    relevance_to_proposition = relevance
  )
}
foundation = list(
  property("G0a", "supported", "The claim and its six scope elements are stated.",
    "csdg_claim() records all six elements.", "They fix the quantity, the models, and the procedure."),
  property("G0b", "supported", "The data cover what the claim names.",
    "The population is defined exactly; there is no measurement error or preprocessing.",
    "The claim names no construct and no other population."),
  property("G2", "supported", "Marginal permutation computes the PFI that the claim names.",
    "Squared error and marginal permutation; both models are defined for all inputs.",
    "The claim names the perturbation, so the unrealistic permuted inputs are part of what it describes."),
  property("G5", "supported", "The ordering persists when the quantity is estimated again.",
    "Exact values do not vary.", "The same quantity is computed again.")
)

The decisive property is G6a: only the model differs between the two computations, the claim covers both models, and model B reverses the ordering. The status records the researcher’s judgment under the criterion; the package does not infer it from the numbers.

g6a = property("G6a", "contradicted", "Item 1 has the larger marginal PFI in A and in B.",
  "PFI of item 1 versus item 2: 2 versus 0 in A, 0 versus 2 in B.",
  "Only the model differs between the two computations, and the claim covers both models.",
  criterion = "strict ordering in both models")
evidence_both = c(foundation, list(g6a))

Step 5: Decide and report

The assessment follows a fixed rule: a claim is not met if at least one required property is contradicted; otherwise it is unresolved if at least one is open; otherwise it is met. Favorable results never offset a contradicted property. With the plan, a required gate without evidence would be open.

assessment_both = csdg_adjudicate_claim(evidence_both, claim_applicable = TRUE, plan = plan)
assessment_both
#> <CSDGClaimAdjudication>
#>   Assessment: not met 
#>   Decision options: revise or withhold 
#>   Required properties:
#>    G0a: supported (record)
#>    G0b: supported (record)
#>    G2: supported (record)
#>    G5: supported (record)
#>    G6a: contradicted (record)
#> 
#>   A required property is contradicted; favorable results never offset it.
stopifnot(identical(assessment_both$assessment, "not_met"),
  identical(assessment_both$decision_options, c("revise", "withhold")))

The original claim is not met; it faces contrary evidence and is revised. The revised claim, restricted to model A, is a new claim with its own record and assessment. It was written after the results were seen, so its assessment is exploratory.

claim_a = csdg_claim_revision(
  claim_both, id = "model_a", claim_version = "C1", revision_relation = "narrower",
  statement = "Under marginal permutation, model A relies more on item 1 than on item 2.",
  model = "fitted_model",
  provenance = list(origin = "retrospective_exploratory", date = "2026-09-26",
    time_basis = "date of the example",
    selection_basis = "restriction chosen after the comparison of A and B", evidence_ids = "both_models_G6a")
)
plan_a = csdg_gate_plan(claim_a, measurement, explanation)
stopifnot(identical(plan_a[required == TRUE, gate_id], c("G0a", "G0b", "G2", "G5")))
g2_a = property("G2", "supported",
  "Marginal PFI with squared error in model A is larger for item 1, and the wording names the perturbation.",
  "2 versus 0; conditional PFI 0 versus 0.",
  "The computation uses the model, perturbation, and loss that the claim names.",
  criterion = "strict ordering of the exact values; qualifier in the wording")
evidence_a = c(foundation[c(1L, 2L, 4L)], list(g2_a))
assessment_a = csdg_adjudicate_claim(evidence_a, claim_applicable = TRUE, plan = plan_a)
assessment_a$assessment
#> [1] "met"
stopifnot(identical(assessment_a$assessment, "met"), identical(assessment_a$decision_options, "retain"))

The revised claim is met (exploratory) and retained. Narrowing a claim can reuse the evidence for the narrower scope. The record compares the revised claim with its predecessor in two ways: for each scope element, whether the new scope is the same, narrower, broader, or incomparable; and, separately, whether the revised claim follows from its predecessor. Here it does: a claim about both models is universal, so it implies the claim about model A (a logical weakening). The package stores this argument; it does not prove it.

relation = csdg_claim_relation(
  claim_both, claim_a,
  coordinate_relations = c(quantity = "same", model = "narrower", procedure = "same", data = "same",
    meaning = "same", use = "same"),
  rationale = "The claim about models A and B is restricted to model A; everything else is unchanged.",
  proposition_relation = "logical_weakening",
  proposition_rationale = "A claim that holds for every model in {A, B} holds for A.",
  revision_kind = "logical_weakening"
)
knitr::kable(relation$scope)
element parent_value claim_value relation
quantity marginal PFI with squared error: increase in expected squared error when one item is permuted marginal PFI with squared error: increase in expected squared error when one item is permuted same
model several_models fitted_model narrower
procedure each item permuted independently of the other item and the outcome; 20 permutations per held-out fold of a 5-fold cross-validation each item permuted independently of the other item and the outcome; 20 permutations per held-out fold of a 5-fold cross-validation same
data population Z ~ N(0, 1), item 1 = item 2 = outcome = Z; 10,000 simulated observations population Z ~ N(0, 1), item 1 = item 2 = outcome = Z; 10,000 simulated observations same
meaning model_description model_description same
use scientific description scientific description same

A met claim holds relative to the listed required properties; it is not a certificate that every relevant property was identified.

An unresolved claim: an unresolved threat

The second part applies the steps to a fitted mlr3 learner. The generated data contain 180 observations and ten candidate predictors; the two predictors of the task were chosen by screening all ten on the full sample, before the cross-validation. The claim uses the predictions, so held-out performance (G1) is required.

set.seed(42)
candidates = as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(180 * 10), ncol = 10, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("x", 1:10))))
outcome = factor(rbinom(180, 1, plogis(1.5 * candidates$x1 - candidates$x2)), levels = c(0, 1))
screening = sapply(candidates, function(x) abs(cor(x, as.numeric(outcome))))
selected = names(sort(screening, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2]
selected
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
dat = data.frame(candidates[selected], y = outcome)
task_screened = as_task_classif(dat, target = "y", positive = "1", id = "screened")
learner = lrn("classif.log_reg", predict_type = "prob")
claim_predict = csdg_claim(
  id = "learner_predicts",
  statement = "The logistic regression learner predicts the outcome better than a model without predictors.",
  claim_type = "predictive_performance",
  quantity = "held-out AUC of the learner and of a model without predictors",
  model = "learner",
  procedure = "3-fold cross-validation; the learner is refitted in each training fold",
  data = "180 generated observations; two predictors screened from ten candidates on the full sample",
  meaning = "model_description", use = "scientific description",
  unit = "generated observation", population = "the generated sample"
)
measurement_screened = csdg_measurement(
  outcome = "y", predictors = selected, data_source = "generated in this vignette",
  sample_definition = "all 180 rows", unit = "generated observation", outcome_scale = "binary factor",
  missingness = "none", preprocessing = "screening of ten candidates by correlation with the outcome",
  verification = list(status = "author_reviewed", artifact = "the generating code of this vignette")
)
csdg_gate_plan(claim_predict, measurement_screened)[required == TRUE, gate_id]
#> [1] "G0a" "G0b" "G1"

The criterion for G1 translates “better than a model without predictors” into a margin with a source and a rationale.

config = csdg_config(
  seed = 42L, resampling = list(folds = 3L, repeats = 1L),
  performance = list(minimum_baseline_improvement = 0.05),
  criteria = list(performance.minimum_baseline_improvement = list(
    source = "translated from the claim",
    rationale = "\"Better\" means a held-out AUC at least 0.05 above that of the model without predictors."
  ))
)
audit_predict = csdg_audit(task_screened, learner, claim_predict, measurement_screened, config = config)
knitr::kable(csdg_report_card(audit_predict)[required == TRUE, .(gate_id, gate_name, status, summary)])
gate_id gate_name status summary
G0a Specification supported The versioned claim states its six scope elements (quantity, model, procedure, data, meaning, use), population, and setting.
G0b Measurement and data supported Measurement, sampling, missingness, and preprocessing are documented with a review artifact.
G1 Predictive performance supported Held-out performance is supported under all prespecified criteria.

The audit supports the G1 property under its criterion. But the predictors were selected on the same data outside the cross-validation, so the held-out values could be optimistic: a specific and plausible, but unquantified, problem. It is an unresolved threat to the G1 property, which is therefore open until a nested analysis quantifies the optimism.

threat = csdg_evidence_record(
  "G1", TRUE, "unresolved_threat",
  required_property = "Held-out performance is not inflated by predictor selection.",
  observation = "The predictors were selected on the same data outside the cross-validation.",
  rationale = "The optimism was not quantified; a nested analysis that repeats the screening in each training fold would resolve it."
)
report_predict = csdg_claim_report(audit_predict, evidence = list(threat))
knitr::kable(report_predict[, .(claim_id, assessment, decision_options, supported_gates, open_gates, threat_gates)])
claim_id assessment decision_options supported_gates open_gates threat_gates
learner_predicts unresolved revise or withhold G0a, G0b G1 G1 
stopifnot(identical(report_predict$assessment, "unresolved"))

The claim is unresolved. It lacks evidence, which a nested analysis or new data could supply; until then, it is withheld and, where it matters, reported as not established.

The same learner: a met claim with the audit

A model description of the same learner, “The logistic regression learner relies on both selected predictors,” requires G2 and G5; held-out performance is context, and the predictor selection bears on it only through performance, which this claim does not interpret. The audit computes the diagnostics: dependence and observed support for G2, and held-out PFI in every fold for G5. It cannot judge whether the procedure computes the quantity that the claim names, so G2 stays open until the researcher records it.

claim_relies = csdg_claim(
  id = "learner_relies",
  statement = "The logistic regression learner relies on both selected predictors.",
  claim_type = "global_explanation",
  quantity = "held-out log-loss increase under marginal permutation of each predictor",
  model = "learner",
  procedure = "3-fold cross-validation; 20 marginal permutations per predictor and held-out fold",
  data = "180 generated observations with the two screened predictors",
  meaning = "model_description", use = "scientific description",
  unit = "generated observation", population = "the generated sample"
)
explanation_screened = csdg_explanation(method_ids = "pfi", scope = "global", target = "held-out log loss",
  perturbation = list(type = "marginal", distribution = "assessment rows in each fold"))
config_relies = csdg_config(seed = 42L, resampling = list(folds = 3L, repeats = 1L),
  stability = list(pfi_repetitions = 20L, top_k = 2L))
audit = csdg_audit(task_screened, learner, claim_relies, measurement_screened, explanation_screened, config = config_relies)
report_card = csdg_report_card(audit)
stopifnot(!any(report_card$status == "error"))
stopifnot(identical(report_card[gate_id == "G1", status], "context"))
knitr::kable(report_card[, .(gate_id, gate_name, required, evidence_role, status, diagnostic_status)])
gate_id gate_name required evidence_role status diagnostic_status
G0a Specification TRUE required_property supported supported
G0b Measurement and data TRUE required_property supported supported
G1 Predictive performance FALSE context context open
G2 Procedure TRUE required_property open open
G3a Calibration FALSE context not_required not_required
G3b Decisions FALSE context not_required not_required
G4 Local fidelity FALSE context not_required not_required
G5 Stability TRUE required_property open open
G6a Models FALSE context not_required not_required
G6b Settings FALSE context not_required not_required
G7a Subgroups FALSE context not_required not_required
G7b Users FALSE context not_required not_required 
pfi_learner = audit$artifacts$pfi$per_iteration
knitr::kable(pfi_learner[, .(iteration, feature_group, importance, monte_carlo_se)], digits = 4)
iteration feature_group importance monte_carlo_se
1 x1 0.2245 0.0115
1 x2 0.0596 0.0070
2 x1 0.2999 0.0193
2 x2 0.0831 0.0102
3 x1 0.2046 0.0171
3 x2 0.1106 0.0084

Held-out performance (G1) is computed and reported as context: it has no property status, and its computed result (diagnostic_status) never changes the assessment. The criterion for G5, positive PFI in every fold beyond twice its Monte Carlo standard error, translates “relies on” into numbers. The two predictors were generated independently, so permuted inputs are realistic (G2).

stopifnot(all(pfi_learner$importance > 2 * pfi_learner$monte_carlo_se))
g2_learner = property("G2", "supported",
  "Held-out marginal permutation computes the log-loss increase that the claim names.",
  "Permutation within each held-out fold; the predictors are independent, so permuted inputs are realistic.",
  "The computation uses the learner, perturbation, and loss that the claim names.")
g5_learner = property("G5", "supported", "Both predictors increase held-out log loss in every fold.",
  sprintf("PFI above twice its Monte Carlo standard error in all %d folds for both predictors.",
    length(unique(pfi_learner$iteration))),
  "Folds vary the training and evaluation data while the learner and perturbation stay fixed.",
  criterion = "PFI > 2 Monte Carlo standard errors in every fold")
report_relies = csdg_claim_report(audit, evidence = list(g2_learner, g5_learner))
knitr::kable(report_relies[, .(claim_id, assessment, decision_options, supported_gates, open_gates)])
claim_id assessment decision_options supported_gates open_gates
learner_relies met retain G0a, G0b, G2, G5 
stopifnot(identical(report_relies$assessment, "met"))

Counterevidence, context, errors, and claims outside the evaluation

Established counterevidence is a demonstrated problem, such as a coding error shown to affect the result. It contradicts the property it bears on, so an otherwise met claim is not met. Context is reported but never changes the assessment. A computation error leaves the property open, not contradicted, and a whole claim is not_applicable only if it is explicitly placed outside the evaluation, with a rationale.

coding_error = csdg_evidence_record(
  "G2", TRUE, "established_counterevidence",
  required_property = "Held-out marginal permutation computes the log-loss increase that the claim names.",
  observation = "Illustration: the two predictor columns were swapped before the PFI computation.",
  relevance_to_proposition = "The swap changes which predictor each reported value refers to.",
  rationale = "A coding error shown to affect the result."
)
grouped = csdg_evidence_record("G5", TRUE, "context", result_direction = "descriptive",
  rationale = "Grouped PFI of both predictors is reported for comparison; it does not bear on each predictor.")
computation = tryCatch(stop("Illustrative computation error"), error = conditionMessage)
failed = csdg_evidence_record("G2", TRUE, "required_property", status = "open", availability = "unavailable",
  rationale = computation)
stopifnot(
  identical(csdg_claim_report(audit, evidence = list(g2_learner, g5_learner, coding_error))$assessment, "not_met"),
  identical(csdg_claim_report(audit, evidence = list(g2_learner, g5_learner, grouped))$assessment, "met"),
  identical(csdg_claim_report(audit, evidence = list(failed, g5_learner))$assessment, "unresolved"),
  identical(csdg_adjudicate_claim(list(), claim_applicable = FALSE,
    applicability_rationale = "The claim is outside this evaluation.")$assessment, "not_applicable")
)

Export, reload, and verify

The audit bundle contains the claim report of the audit claim, now assessed by the decision rule from the audit diagnostics alone: without the researcher’s records, G2 and G5 are open, so the claim is unresolved. The explicit assessments of all four claims, with the researcher’s records, are written next to the bundle, not into it, so the bundle’s checksum manifest stays valid; a receipt names the file, its SHA-256 checksum, the bundle, and all claim identifiers.

export_root = tempfile("csdg_walkthrough_")
dir.create(export_root)
audit_bundle = csdg_export(audit, path = export_root)
explicit = list(
  package_version = as.character(packageVersion("mlr3autoiml")),
  claims = list(claim_both, claim_a, claim_predict, claim_relies),
  evidence = list(evidence_both, evidence_a, list(threat), list(g2_learner, g5_learner)),
  assessments = list(assessment_both$assessment, assessment_a$assessment, report_predict$assessment,
    report_relies$assessment),
  decisions = c("revise", "retain", "withhold", "retain"),
  reported_claims = c("Revised to the claim about model A.", claim_a$statement,
    "Withheld: not established.", claim_relies$statement),
  relation = relation
)
assessment_path = file.path(export_root, "explicit_assessments.json")
jsonlite::write_json(explicit, assessment_path, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE, null = "null", na = "null")
receipt = list(
  assessment_file = basename(assessment_path),
  assessment_sha256 = digest::digest(file = assessment_path, algo = "sha256"),
  audit_bundle = basename(audit_bundle),
  claim_ids = c(claim_both$id, claim_a$id, claim_predict$id, claim_relies$id)
)
jsonlite::write_json(receipt, file.path(export_root, "receipt.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
read_back = jsonlite::read_json(assessment_path)
read_receipt = jsonlite::read_json(file.path(export_root, "receipt.json"))
bundle_report = read.csv(file.path(audit_bundle, "claim_report.csv"))
stopifnot(identical(vapply(read_back$claims, `[[`, character(1L), "id"), receipt$claim_ids),
  identical(unlist(read_back$assessments), c("not_met", "met", "unresolved", "met")),
  identical(unlist(read_back$decisions), c("revise", "retain", "withhold", "retain")),
  identical(read_receipt$assessment_sha256, digest::digest(file = assessment_path, algo = "sha256")),
  identical(bundle_report$assessment, "unresolved"), identical(bundle_report$open_gates, "G2, G5"))
cat("Export and read-back verified for all four claims.\n")
#> Export and read-back verified for all four claims.
# A caller can retain this synthetic-only bundle without changing the tutorial.
keep = Sys.getenv("CSDG_VIGNETTE_EXPORT_DIR")
if (nzchar(keep)) {
  dir.create(keep, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(file.copy(list.files(export_root, full.names = TRUE), keep, recursive = TRUE)))
}

The applications in the article

In SHILD, the claim that XGBoost relies mainly on self-rated health and depressed mood is met (exploratory) and retained, as are the claims that apparent fidelity overstates how accurately the local surrogates reproduce the model on new points and that, for this rare outcome, surrogates fitted on the log-odds scale reproduce it more accurately. The claim that explanations of individual predictions can guide follow-up decisions is not met, because the stability property (G5) is contradicted, and is withheld. The revised population claim about the information that the two items carry is unresolved, because agreement among similarly accurate learners (G6a) is open, and is withheld.

In PISA, the claim that the five most important predictors of XGBoost are the same for every plausible value is met (a sanity check). The claim that three similarly accurate learners have the same five most important predictors is not met and is revised; the claim that ridge regression relies far more on socioeconomic indices than XGBoost and random forest do is not met and is withheld. In the confirmatory stage, four of five claims are met. The article and its supplement report the records, criteria, and numbers.

For further diagnostics, see the help pages ?csdg_audit, ?csdg_local_fidelity_audit (the fitted local surrogate is described in ?csdg_diagnostics, section “Local surrogate”), ?csdg_learner_pfi_interval, and ?csdg_importance_agreement.
